prompt:
Use case: stylized-concept.
Asset type: ONE individual square PNG for a 30-pair ships memory game.
Primary request: a beautiful, accurate, finished COLOUR SKETCH of the single real named vessel below.
Input image: the aircraft image is ONLY the approved drawing STYLE and warm ivory PAPER reference. Do NOT draw an aircraft. Match its fine visible coloured-pencil strokes, delicate graphite contours, selective cross-hatching and restrained transparent watercolour modelling, softly lit from upper left. Expert maritime illustrator, richly finished yet visibly hand drawn, natural colours, paper highlights. No photographic, CGI, toy, cartoon or vector look.
Backdrop: uniform warm ivory drawing paper, subtle fine grain, otherwise BLANK edge to edge. No scenery, sky, ocean, horizon, waves, wake, ground, cast shadow or decorative wash. Show the vessel as a clean waterline portrait: only its above-water hull, with a neat lower waterline edge on blank paper.
Composition: SQUARE 1:1, at least 1024px. Exactly ONE complete ship, centred, with moderate three-quarter foreshortening so the long side and distinctive silhouette are readable. All extremities including bowsprit, mast tops, sails, cranes, stern and lifeboats must fit in the central 72% of BOTH dimensions. At least 14% completely blank paper on EVERY side. Do not enlarge it to fill the page. Keep the vessel upright with vertical masts; varied compass headings and viewing sides across this collection, NEVER a rolled or tipped ship.
Text: none. No names, letters, numbers, hull identifiers, logos, flags bearing symbols, labels, caption, signature, watermark or card border. Identification through major shape and colours. No crew, passengers, other vessels or objects.
Historical treatment: portray the vessel intact in its working heyday even if it was later sunk or retired. No damage, sinking, combat, smoke or explosions.
Specific vessel, identifying details and requested view: RMS Titanic, in 1912. Iconic long black ocean-liner hull with a thin ochre/gold sheer line and a narrow red antifouling strip at waterline, white tiered superstructure, EXACTLY FOUR evenly spaced buff-yellow funnels with black caps, two slender masts, fine tan deck details and white lifeboats. The fourth funnel still present. No lettering. Slightly elevated port-bow three-quarter view, bow toward lower LEFT, long stern toward upper right, modest perspective, broadside still clearly legible. Entire long liner occupies at most 72% of the square width.

edits.prompt: Edit this Titanic illustration only to correct its size on the paper. Preserve the exact four-funnel ship, colours, all geometry, details, viewpoint and beautiful fine coloured-pencil/graphite texture. UNIFORMLY SHRINK the ENTIRE ship including BOTH masts and rigging to 78% of its current size, centred in the same square ivory page. The WHOLE silhouette must occupy no more than 68% of the image width AND height, surrounded by at least 16% completely blank ivory paper on ALL FOUR sides. Fill newly exposed paper seamlessly with exactly the existing paper texture. Do not add text, border, water, shadow, scenery or anything else. This is a scale-and-position correction only.

review: Four funnels, whole intact ship, ivory pencil style and generous safe margin visually reviewed.
